recipes.name: Chicken and Asparagus with Penne Pasta
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch garlic salt, or to taste
1 pinch seasoned salt, or to taste
1 pound fresh asparagus, trimmed and cut crosswise into thirds
1 pinch garlic salt, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Cover a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Spread the chicken breast tenderloins on the baking sheet and sprinkle with garlic salt and seasoned salt.
Bake chicken in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 15 minutes. Set aside; when cool enough to handle, cut tenderloins into bite-size pieces.

Fill a large pot with lightly salted water, bring to a boil, and stir in penne. Cook pasta at a boil, stirring occasionally, until penne are cooked through but still slightly firm, about 11 minutes; drain.
Transfer penne back to cooking pot and stir in butter and Parmesan cheese until pasta is coated.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat; place asparagus into the hot oil and sprinkle with garlic salt. Cook and stir until asparagus are tender, about 7 minutes.
Transfer penne pasta into a large serving bowl and top with asparagus and chicken tenderloin pieces. Lightly mix asparagus and chicken into the pasta to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Asparagus with Penne Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Tender asparagus and chunks of chicken combine with penne pasta in a simple, light, and satisfying main dish.

review.reviewBody: LOVE this recipe! I used whole wheat penne pasta and instead of garlic salt on the chicken i used garlic powder. This is definitely going in my recipe box for future meals!! :)

Excellent!! Instead of garlic salt/ powder I sautéed asparagus with fresh garlic in evo and butter. Next time I will try it with chicken thighs because chicken breast meat is not hubby’s favorite. Try it, you will not be disappointed

Save a step - cook your asparagus with your pasta. Just throw it in the last 4 minutes of cooking. Drain and add butter, Parmesan, chicken (I used leftover from a rotisserie), and I also added a little milk for creaminess and fresh pepper. I like these flavors and did not find it bland at all. Super quick weeknight meal. Literally on the table in 30 minutes.

As I write this review my husband is having his third serving. That definitely earns five stars. I chose to saute the chicken as it was already too warm in my kitchen to warrant turning on the oven. This was very tasty. I did use some extra olive oil and a little pasta water to keep it from drying out. This is a keeper and I'll definitely be making it again!

I love finding new ways to use asparagus so I couldn't wait to try this! I used whole wheat penne, replaced the butter with olive oil and the garlic salt with garlic powder / minced garlic and added black pepper and a touch of cayenne pepper to the chicken before baking. I mixed the cooked chicken in with the asparagus for the last couple minutes in the saute pan then added it all to the pasta. Very good, I'll definitely make it again!

I agree with other reviewers, it’s bland. I will add some heavy cream so that it is a more creamy sauce and I will add red pepper flakes next time to give it some zing. It is a healthy dish which is good.

I sprinkled Zesty Italian Dressing Mix on the chicken tenderloins before baking. I used the tip of adding the asparagus to the penne for the last 4 minutes. Perfect amount of time for us - it’s so easy to cook them too long and end up with mushy asparagus. Otherwise, the recipe was unchanged. I love having a recipe for asparagus! Such a tasty dish. Thanks for the recipe!!
Yummy and easy. I even skipped the baking of the chicken and just sautéed it with the asparagus. One less pan to clean!

This was a quick simple, tasty dish. I added grape tomatoes, halved and fresh garlic at the end of cooking the asparagus. Flavor came from the fresh ingredients. I also sprinkled with a little crushed red pepper. Yum!
It was ok. We added the juice of one lemon to give it some zing.

So it is a very quick & delicious recipe! While cooking the chicken I cooked pasta to save time . Also started cooking asparagus towards end of cooking time for pasta & chicken to also save time rather than doing one step at a time !

As written, it is fairly bland. Next time, I will probably add some minced garlic to the asparagus, possibly a shallot. And a squeeze of lemon over the dish at the end. Probably a little more salt as well.
This recipe is great and easy/quick to make, but I would definitely recommend adding alfredo sauce to it as it was a little dry without a sauce.
Loved it!
Loved this! But next time I would use fresh minced garlic.
We love it. I like to double the asparagus and the parmesan. It is so good that we never have left overs.

It was okay as presented. However, I found that when making it in smaller amounts such as we do for just the two of us I cook the pasta in low sodium chicken broth (14 oz can for 5 oz pasta) then steam the asparagus in the remaining broth.

I made it today with some leftover breast from a smoked chicken and added some fresh basil at the end. Yummy.

Next time I add some fresh mushrooms.

I'm not sure what was missing from this dish, but the flavor was very bland. I even sauteed the asparagus with real diced up garlic cloves and used fresh shredded Asiago cheese as well. No one in my family hated this, but they didn't really enjoyed it either. I have a feeling the leftovers will go to waste. Disappointing!
Too bland. Tried making a Parmesan cream sauce to add flavour but still wasn't flavourful enough.
This is one of the families favorites and it's a keeper! I made it just like the recipe. It was simple and so delicious. Absolutely will make it again!
